records.name: Switzerland
records.summary:
Switzerland is a very safe destination for transgender visitors. Legal gender recognition has worked by self-declaration since January 2022 — a personal declaration before the civil registrar, with no court or medical requirements (binary male/female only; no non-binary marker). Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2022 (approved by referendum), gender-neutral rape law took effect in 2024, and employers have a legal duty of care toward trans employees. General crime is exceptionally low.

The notable legislative shortcoming — flagged by the ILGA Rainbow Map and by the government's own review — is that the criminal hate-crime and hate-speech provision (Article 261bis) covers sexual orientation but not gender identity. So a person targeted specifically for being trans does not benefit from that aggravation in criminal law, though the protections available through employment and constitutional law are broader. Reported hate crimes against LGBTIQ people have risen about fivefold since 2020 (around six per week, but from a low absolute base of ~309 cases in 2024).

The fede

sources.summary: Swiss Federal Office for Gender Equality rights overview: since 1 July 2020 public incitement to hatred, denigration or discrimination on sexual-orientation grounds is punishable under Art. 261bis Criminal Code; 'Marriage for All' has been in force since 1 July 2022 (same-sex marriage, adoption, IVF). Freshness pass confirms both pages current.

EPFL guidance on the Swiss civil status register: since 1 January 2022 any person registered in a Swiss municipality can change their sex marker and/or first name by personal declaration before a civil registrar — a self-declaration route without surgery or court proceedings.

SWI swissinfo (7 Aug 2022): about 350 people had used the simplified self-declaration gender-change process introduced on 1 January 2022 within its first months — early uptake of the new marker-change route.

SWI swissinfo, citing LGBTIQ Helpline monitoring: roughly six anti-LGBTIQ+ hate crimes are reported per week in Switzerland — 309 cases in the reference year, with reports up fivefold since 2020. The main day-to-day safety signal for visitors.

Federal Office for Gender Equality: on 28 January 2026 the Federal Council adopted Switzerland's first National Action Plan against hate crimes against LGBTIQ persons 2026-2030, with three pillars — support and protection of victims, prevention of hate crime, and monitoring of violence; FOGE coordinates implementation.

SWI swissinfo on the same first national action plan (2026): coverage of the government's new measures to protect LGBTQI+ people from hate crimes — dated press corroboration of the federal plan and of the rising-report context that prompted it.

LegalClarity (3 Jun 2026): marriage equality since 1 July 2022 after 64.1% referendum approval; criminal-law protection against sexual-orientation discrimination since July 2020; streamlined legal gender change since January 2022 — 'from marriage equality to gender recognition, but some gaps remain'.

trans welcome (Switzerland) workplace legal framework: employers must protect employees' personal dignity under Art. 328ff. Code of Obligations, concretised for trans people by the Equality Act (GLG); trans staff may use their preferred name and gender at work without any official document change.

records.name: Greece
records.summary:
Greece is a workable destination with a clear law-versus-practice gap. The legal framework is among Europe's strongest — it ranks 7th on the ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map, has banned conversion therapy and intersex infant surgery, has a hate-crime law covering gender identity, and legalised same-sex marriage in 2024 (the first Orthodox-majority country to do so). There are no trans-specific border or bathroom restrictions, and the government is progressive with an improving trajectory.

But the social reality lags the law. A mob of about 150 people assaulted two trans people in Thessaloniki; an European Court of Human Rights case documented police detention and mistreatment of trans sex workers; surveys show Greeks are markedly more avoidant of public LGBTI visibility than the EU average (63% avoid holding hands); and the UK Foreign Office has issued an LGBTQ travel warning for Greece.

Major tourist destinations — Mykonos, Athens's Gazi district, Thessaloniki — are welcoming; outside them the climate is rougher than the law suggests.

sources.summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024): marriage-equality Law 5089/2024 added SOGIESC equal-treatment guarantees in goods/services, education, healthcare and housing; in March a mob of ~150 attacked two trans people in Thessaloniki (21 arrested, 11 minors) followed by a masked attack on counter-protesters; the Orthodox Church officially opposed marriage equality; transphobic comments targeted Eurovision contestants.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025): the ECtHR condemned Greece for detaining an LGBTI Iranian refugee pending deportation (Article 3 violation); a criminal case opened over an online post inciting discrimination against immigrants and LGBTI people; in July the Crete Court of Appeal convicted three French tourists for a 2017 attack.

ECtHR app. 459/16, Koutra and Katzaki v. Greece (judgment 2017): police stopped and mistreated transgender sex workers and their lawyer in Athens in 2013 (street stops, removal from cars); complaints against officers were discontinued — documented police conduct toward visibly trans people.

PinkNews (Apr 2024): the UK Foreign Office updated its Greece travel advice for LGBTQ+ holidaymakers — same-sex relations legal, civil unions since 2015, marriage since Feb 2024 (first Orthodox-majority country), age of consent 15 for all, legal gender change possible; travellers advised to remain alert.

EU FRA LGBTIQ survey III, Greece country sheet (2024): 63% avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (EU-27: 53%); 36% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (EU: 29%); only 35% are open about being LGBTIQ (EU: 51%); 28% felt discriminated at work (EU: 19%).

Outright profile (updated Mar 2026): Greece ranked 7th in Europe on the 2025 Rainbow Map; conversion practices banned for minors and IGM criminalised (2022); employment-discrimination ban on SOGI (2023); Feb 2024 Law 5089/2024 extended equal-treatment grounds (SOGIESC) across social protection, education, healthcare, housing and goods/services alongside marriage equality.

The Press Project (May 2025): TGEU Trans Rights Index & Map 2025 shows backsliding outpacing progress across Europe for the first time; Greece meets 21 of 32 indicators — gaps include age restrictions on name changes, no national action plan, no legal recognition of trans/non-binary parenthood.

Wikipedia overview: same-sex marriage legal since 2024; adoption and foster care; discrimination and hate-speech protections; self-ID gender recognition since 2017; conversion therapy; military service; social conditions including Pride events and homophobic violence.
